surprises.head: Colorado flipped the shot count
surprises.body: New Jersey controls the shot count like almost no one else. Not tonight: Colorado took 70 of the 105 shot attempts at 5-on-5. From how these two usually play, Colorado would expect about 47%. A team strays this far about once every 200 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

surprises.head: Colorado’s power play came alive
surprises.body: New Jersey kills penalties better than most. Not tonight: Colorado’s power play created 16.3 expected goals per 60, against their usual 7.1 (about 6.4 against New Jersey) and a league average of 7.7. A team strays this far about once every 35 games.

story.head: The Avalanche pour it on late
paras: Connor Brown opened the scoring for the Devils shorthanded midway through the first, but Gabriel Landeskog made it 1-1 for Colorado on the power play midway through the second. There were five goals in the third period alone. Nazem Kadri and Parker Kelly scored just over a minute apart early in the period to put the Avalanche up 3-1. Nathan MacKinnon and Jaden Schwartz scored 30 seconds apart with eight minutes left to stretch the lead to 5-1. Brown struck again with four and a half minutes left to make it 5-2, bringing it to 5-2.

The Avalanche carried the play, outshooting the Devils 44-22, and got the result to match. Mackenzie Blackwood made 20 saves for the Avalanche, and Jake Allen stopped 39 of 44 at the other end. By our Swing measure, Artturi Lehkonen had the best night of anyone. The Avs improved to 7-5-1, fourth in the Central, while the Devils fell to 8-5-0, second in the Metropolitan.

items.text: The Devils’ four-game winning streak is over.
Artturi Lehkonen has a point in eight straight games.
Nathan MacKinnon scored again against New Jersey, and has seven goals in eight games against them since 2023-24.
Arseny Gritsyuk’s six-game point streak ended.
